# FERB.app (notch UI, intro, sounds) (area `app`)

The Mac app the owner uses: notch, chat, settings, setup intro, orb, sounds, preview window, playground. The owner's side; talks to the daemon only through its RPC.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **APP-500** (owner): First install is a short, interactive introduction that makes FERB feel like it belongs on the Mac: taught through small interactions, not slides, with the real notch central so setup feels like using the product; capable and warm, never cartoonish or theatrical. In one continuous tour a new user meets FERB, connects it, sees what it can do on their Mac, learns to control it and to bring it back, ending in the notch. The intro shows existing capabilities only; outside references are studied for principles, never their assets or flow.
- **APP-501** (owner): The notch is FERB's home and voice: it swells down to speak and shrinks back when done, and all of FERB's tour words come from it except a short instruction beside the orb. When FERB shows a place on screen, a small glass orb (an iridescent band inside that ripples while FERB listens or waits) drips off the notch in a liquid split, flies there, helps with the step, hops when the step is done, flies home and melts back; the notch swells once as it takes it back.
- **APP-502** (owner): In the tour FERB's lines are text in the notch, never read aloud; the only sound in the tour comes from FERB's sound family.
- **APP-503** (agent): While the orb helps with a step, a small frosted bubble next to it carries one instruction line (e.g. "Drag me into this list") and a reason line.
- **APP-504** (agent): Springs with a perceptual duration of about 0.35-0.5 s: opening with a small bounce (0.15-0.3), closing and dismissal critically damped (bounce 0), morphs snappy. Every animation is interruptible and retargetable mid-flight, keeping its velocity. Decorative animations last at most 2 s and the user never waits on one. Content stays concentric with the notch; the notch and the orb split and merge as liquid (metaball). Reduce Motion: springs become cross-fades and the orb fades in beside its target instead of flying.
- **APP-505** (owner): The tour runs: 1 Meet (the notch says hello in one or two lines; the full sound logo plays once); 2 Sign in; 3 Allow all, guided; 4 Pair all browsers; 5 FERB's own email, optional; 6 Try: look, tell, show the journey; 7 Control, taught by doing with today's controls (double-tap right Option, hold to talk, Control-Option-Space, stopping a task, pausing FERB), each done once; 8 Back to the notch: FERB small in the notch with one line on how to bring it back. Replay intro is in Settings.
- **APP-506** (agent): During Meet FERB installs its background service silently; if macOS asks for the Login Items approval (serviceNeedsApproval), the orb guides that one System Settings visit before sign-in.
- **APP-507** (agent): Sign in offers Codex or Claude first, with "Other ways to connect" for an Anthropic, OpenAI or Google API key. As soon as sign-in succeeds FERB starts the Mac scan (MEM-13) in the background so it is ready by the Try beat; a cancelled or failed sign-in never starts it.
- **APP-508** (owner): Every permission FERB asks at setup is required; setup grants them through one Allow all, and Automation stays per app at first use. Required grants still missing at the end bring setup back at the next launch.
- **APP-509** (agent): After an update a required grant counts as missing for FERB.app's own rows too (Notifications, Microphone), and the daemon's setup.finish checks every row before recording setup done.
- **APP-510** (owner): Allow all starts a guided sequence. For a list pane FERB opens the exact pane and the orb docks beside System Settings holding a real draggable FERB icon, follows the window and hides when Settings isn't in front; a request-style permission gets one notch line, then the system prompt. A grant counts only when the system confirms it, with a real check where the API can be stale, polled about every 1.5 s, never inferred from a drop. A grant that needs a restart restarts that part without losing the tour's place.
- **APP-511** (owner): The extension is added to every installed browser and one Pair all button pairs every profile at once; a per-profile Pair stays for those who want it. In the tour the orb flies to each browser's own "turn on" prompt if one appears.
- **APP-512** (owner): One beat offers FERB its own email for sign-ups and searches, now or later. Skipping costs nothing: it stays in Settings and FERB asks again the first time a task needs it.
- **APP-513** (owner): FERB says in one or two specific lines what it saw from the scan, then suggests two first tasks that fit this user, of different kinds where possible (one on the Mac or in files, one in the browser); with no clear scan, two general tasks. The user picks one and "Show the other one" previews the second. The preview shows the plan and the answer-in-steps rows and cards in the real chat UI, each marked as a preview, while the orb flies to the apps it would use. Nothing is clicked, typed, sent, opened or changed.
- **APP-514** (agent): A "Do it for real" choice taken in the Try beat starts as a normal real task, with its usual questions, only after the tour ends at Home. Stopping is practised in the Control beat on the Try beat's preview, replayed as a running preview.
- **APP-515** (agent): A resumed tour whose background service is down waits on "Getting my background part ready…" until the daemon answers or the owner skips.
- **APP-516** (owner): The tour can be skipped at any point, resumes at the same beat after a quit, and replays from Settings. A skip tears down everything the tour drew or said (orb, sound, drag card) at once and leaves the required steps still missing (service, sign-in, permissions) in the compact window. The app opts out of automatic termination during the tour.
- **APP-517** (owner): An install that finished setup never sees the tour (Settings offers Replay intro); one that finished setup but is missing grants gets only those beats plus Home. An install that never finished setup and predates the intro gets the full tour, as a first run.
- **APP-518** (owner): On a Mac without a hardware notch a virtual notch pill plays the notch's role, in the tour too: the orb launches from it on FERB's screen.
- **APP-519** (owner): The intro design fixes behaviour, flow, motion rules and the sound system; visual polish is the owner's, done in the Swift app. The look and feel is iterated in the intro playground, which runs the real intro code with everything behind it faked.
- **APP-520** (owner): FERB has an original, recognisable family of sounds sharing one character, each meaning one thing and recognisable without looking. A sound logo (full, tour only) seeds short derived cues, quieter and shorter the more often they play; needs you is the loudest everyday cue. Every sound has a visual twin, so FERB is fully understandable with sound off. FERB honours "Play user interface sound effects" and the alert volume, and never plays music under the tour.
- **APP-521** (owner): FERB makes a sound only for big events and where it is needed. Working is silent; there are no hover, typing or repeating progress sounds.
- **APP-522** (owner): In the tour sound is attached to FERB's position and movement, not a soundtrack: at the notch while FERB speaks, with the orb while it is out, home with it.
- **APP-523** (agent): Mono sources are placed from the notch's and the orb's frames: pan = clamp((x / screenWidth - 0.5) x 1.2, -0.6, 0.6), the notch at 0; distance from the notch lowers gain by at most 3 dB and adds a low-pass, never elevation or Doppler. HRTF (AVAudioEnvironmentNode) only when headphones are the output, equal-power pan otherwise. The engine stays warm and compensates output latency; no tight sync is promised on Bluetooth. Meaning never depends on position.
- **APP-524** (owner): The Crystal family, synthesised from code under the owner's direction with no samples, ships as FERB's own sounds; hiring a sound designer stays optional for later. No library loops or sample-library content, no game or film music.
- **APP-525** (owner): Google Material's "hero" clip (first launch) and "notification, high intensity" ship under CC BY 4.0 with their credit (Settings → About, Resources/Sounds/CREDITS.md, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, the app's ThirdPartyNotices.txt): the one exception to the family's own sounds.
- **APP-526** (owner): The tour and every everyday event play FERB's family through one engine, replacing the macOS system sounds. Every sound has its own switch: on by default for needs you, error, done, notification, listening start and end, and the tour; off for summon and paused. Standard is the default intensity, Subtle the choice in Settings. The master volume stays at 0.18; the existing master switch and volume carry over on upgrade.
- **APP-527** (owner): FERB has no magnetic docking sound; its setting is gone and an old value is cleared on upgrade.
- **APP-528** (owner): While another app is using the microphone (a call, dictation elsewhere), FERB plays no sound except needs you, at Subtle; the notch still shows everything. FERB's own dictation never counts as a call. Focus, quiet hours, screen sharing and media playing get no rule.
- **APP-529** (owner): As FERB first starts, Google Material's "hero" clip plays once; then no background sound until the notch plays the sound logo, which never starts before the clip ends. A replay or resume plays no clip.
- **APP-530** (owner): Bright Crystal glass plays the sound logo (Open fifth, tour only), summon, listening start and end, and done. Paused (one damped tap) and error (a sinking "uh-oh" onto a hollow B minor) use the same glass finger-damped: duller, an octave lower, no strike, so they never sound like completion.
- **APP-531** (owner): Needs you is "One ping": a single Crystal note on A (the unresolved dominant) left to ring; the loudest everyday cue.
- **APP-532** (owner): Material's "notification, high intensity" plays for every notification FERB gives: its macOS banners and the reminders, schedules and notices that arrive in the notch chat. A notice shown both as a banner and in the notch sounds once: the banner carries it and the notch stays silent for it.
- **APP-534** (owner): The orb's drip-off (the old flight sound: one singing-glass swell, about 1.2 s) plays when it sets off, the hop when a step succeeds, the melt-back when it arrives at its target and when it comes home. There is no flight sound and no separate landing sound.
